sanskrit_verse: भूशुद्धिर् मार्जनाद् दाहात् कालाद् गोक्रमणात् तथा । सेकाद् उल्लेखनाल् लेपाद् गृहं मार्जनलेपनात् ॥
transliteration: bhūśuddhir mārjanād dāhāt kālād gokramaṇāt tathā / sekād ullekhanāl lepād gṛhaṃ mārjanalepanāt //
sph_interpretive_translation: Purification of land arises through sweeping, burning, time, grazing of cows, watering, scraping, plastering, and cleaning or smearing of houses.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in natural processes aligned with cosmic order
Causation follows sequential purification actions rooted in dharma
Capacity-based responsibility lies in maintaining purity through action
Restoration logic operates through repetition of purificatory acts
Consciousness alignment occurs when environment reflects inner cleanliness
executable_legal_axioms: IF property is impure THEN initiate sequence: sweep, burn, irrigate, cow-graze, scrape, plaster, clean OR smear
IF dwelling lacks purity THEN execute cleansing cycle until sensory perception confirms purity
IF individual controls space THEN that individual bears capacity-responsibility for its purification
IF contamination spreads THEN halt causal agents AND apply purification protocol recursively
IF consciousness perceives uncleanness THEN trigger environmental purification subroutine
supreme_court_application: In adjudication concerning environmental or domestic sanctity, the court shall mandate purification protocols as defined by dharma rather than impose punitive measures. The threshold of responsibility is determined by proximity to the contaminated domain and awareness of causal disruption.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that purity is a function of specific acts; anupūrvaśaḥ ensures sequential restoration without blame; proportional responsibility aligns with control over the affected area; non-punitive reality prevails because impurity is neutralized through prescribed action, not suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate purification completion process via ritualized environmental cleansing
Assign responsibility assumption protocol to caretakers of defiled spaces
Restore capacity through guided repetition of purifying acts
Reintegrate integrity by verifying sensory confirmation of restored purity
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. Land and habitation purified according to Sanatana injunctions. Justice executed not through punishment but through conscious restoration. Reality affirmed as non-punitive. Consciousness stands as ultimate adjudicator.
